title: Trigger squeeze and breathing
subtitle: Placing the finger, avoiding the flinch, controlling your breath

lines: This episode covers trigger squeeze and breathing.
The book says the correct placement of the trigger finger onto the trigger is of great importance.

lines.text: Here's the trigger, inside the trigger guard.
The trigger finger must not be too far through the trigger guard.

scenes.heading: Placing the trigger finger
bullets: Use the first digit of the trigger finger
Any part of the first digit
From the button-pushing part to the first joint

lines.text: The first digit of the trigger finger must be used to squeeze the trigger.
You can use any part of the first digit of the finger.
That's between the part of the finger you would use to push a button, and up to the first joint.

lines: The book says this is probably the single most important fundamental of shooting.

scenes.heading: Correct trigger placement
scenes.caption: Correct trigger placement, from the side and from behind
lines: Here you can see the correct placement of the trigger finger.
The book shows it from the side, and from behind.

scenes.heading: Incorrect trigger placement
scenes.caption: Incorrect: too much finger through the trigger guard
lines: Here the shooter is extending too much of the trigger finger through the trigger guard.
This will cause you to pull the gun to one side when the trigger is squeezed.

scenes.definition: Also known as trigger control: an even amount of pressure on the trigger from start to finish.
lines: Trigger squeeze is also known as trigger control.
An even amount of pressure must be applied to the trigger from start to finish.
You must concentrate on pulling the trigger straight back.

scenes.definition: Jerking the trigger, so the shot appears low on the target.
lines: Do not jerk the trigger, or your shot will appear low on the target.
This is known as flinching.
Many shooters flinch when they are not comfortable with the recoil of the firearm.
Flinching also occurs when the shooter anticipates the shot going off.

rule.text: You should not know the precise time when the gun will fire. It should take you by surprise.

lines: You should not know the precise time when the gun will fire.
It should actually take you by surprise.
And when you squeeze the trigger, it must not disrupt your sight picture or sight alignment.

scenes.heading: Practising trigger squeeze
bullets: A drill round, or dummy round, in the firearm
Dry fire while looking at the sights
lines: A good method for practising is to use a drill round, also called a dummy round, in the firearm.
This protects the firing pin.
Then dry fire while looking at the sights, to see how steady you can hold the firearm.

scenes.heading: Breathing
bullets: Take up the slack on the trigger
lines: To shoot accurately, you must control your breathing whilst squeezing the trigger.
This is done in order to eliminate muscle tremors.
The book gives the recommended way to do this in five steps.

lines.text: One: take up the slack on the trigger.
Two: take a normal breath in.

rule.text: Do not hold your breath for too long before squeezing the trigger.

lines: Do not hold your breath for too long before squeezing the trigger.
This will cause you to start shaking, as you begin to run out of oxygen.
You may find that after you have fired the shot, you have to breathe in.
If so, you are holding your breath for too long, or taking too long to squeeze the trigger.

scenes.question: If a person is flinching, what are they doing?
options: Jerking the trigger, so the shot goes low
lines: Here's a question from your formative exam.
If a person is flinching, what are they doing?
reveal: They are jerking the trigger, and the shot will appear low on the target.
Shooters flinch when they are not comfortable with the recoil, or when they anticipate the shot going off.

scenes.question: When do you complete the trigger squeeze?
lines: One more.
In the breathing steps, when do you complete the trigger squeeze?
reveal: Take up the slack, take a normal breath in, breathe halfway out, complete the squeeze, then breathe completely out.

points: The first digit of the trigger finger
Slack, in, halfway out, squeeze, out
lines: So, squeeze the trigger with the first digit of the trigger finger.
Apply an even amount of pressure, and pull straight back.
Jerking the trigger is flinching, and the shot appears low.
The shot should take you by surprise.
And for breathing: take up the slack, breathe in, breathe halfway out, squeeze, then breathe completely out.
